groups.title: Tablet (402300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes caused by a cold or by allergic and vasomotor rhinitis, and of nasal congestion caused by sinusitis.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet every 4 hours, and do not exceed 6 tablets in 24 hours. Ages 6 years to under 12 years: take 1/2 tablet every 4 hours, and do not exceed 3 tablets in 24 hours. For those under 6 years of age, follow the instructions of a doctor.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to amine sympathomimetics or antihistamines; if you are breast-feeding; if you have severe high blood pressure, severe coronary artery disease, narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, peptic ulcer, asthma, emphysema or chronic lung disease; or if you are short of breath or have difficulty breathing.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have difficulty breathing such as chronic bronchitis, heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia.

If symptoms do not improve within 7 days, or if a high fever occurs at the same time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor. Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.

People being treated with an MAO inhibitor and people being given a sedative or a tranquilliser must not take this medicine. Avoid alcoholic drinks while taking it.

Fear, anxiety, tension, tremor, weakness, pallor, difficulty breathing, difficulty passing urine, insomnia, hallucination, convulsions, central nervous system depression, arrhythmia, dizziness, cardiovascular collapse with low blood pressure, rapid heartbeat, palpitations, headache, nausea, thirst, weakness, loss of appetite, vomiting, nervousness, excessive urine volume, heartburn, double vision, difficulty passing urine, dermatitis, drowsiness or excitement may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Temporary relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes from a cold or allergic and vasomotor rhinitis, and nasal congestion from sinusitis

groups.title: Capsule (727000ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for bowel regulation, constipation, loose stools, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen and abnormal fermentation in the intestine.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 4/3 capsule per dose. Ages 8 years to under 11 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, before meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Bowel regulation, constipation, loose stools, fullness in the abdomen and abnormal intestinal fermentation

groups.title: Tablet (D14700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Tablet (566833ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of selenium in people with selenium deficiency that cannot be made up by nutritional intake.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet (100 micrograms as selenium), 1 time in 1 day; the dose may be increased to a maximum of 2 tablets (200 micrograms as selenium) in 1 day. Take this medicine with water, without chewing it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have selenium toxicity; or if you have hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase deficiency.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a reducing agent such as vitamin C. If you want to take vitamin C, take it separately with an interval of about 4 hours from this medicine. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, vomiting or allergy occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (308000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammatory swelling after surgery and injury and in milk stasis.
groups.usage: Adults: on the first day take 2 tablets per dose, 4 times in 1 day. After that, as a maintenance dose, take 1 tablet per dose, 4 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have a blood clotting disorder; or if you have severe liver impairment or kidney impairment.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given an anticoagulant.

If rash, reddening of the skin, diarrhoea, constipation, loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, nausea or vomiting occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, a tendency to bleed such as nosebleed or blood in the sputum occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A04700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of heartburn associated with excess stomach acid and a burning sensation in the stomach.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have difficulty taking it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 15 years of age; if you have unexplained weight loss or persistent abdominal pain; if you have kidney disease; if you are on haemodialysis; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with a stomach medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antacid, atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol, chloroquine, a tetracycline antibiotic, diflunisal, digoxin, a diphosphonate, fexofenadine, iron (salts), a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, sodium fluoride, a glucocorticoid, indometacin, ketoconazole, lansoprazole, a phenothiazine antiepileptic, penicillamine, a phosphate, thyroxine (reduced absorption of the medicine) or a salicylate.

Occasionally nausea, diarrhoea or headache, and rarely anaphylaxis, enzyme abnormalities, constipation, loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, flatulence, vomiting, thirst, rash, itching, urticaria, peeling of the skin, fatigue, jaundice, hepatitis, angioneurotic oedema, joint pain or muscle cramps may occur.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A18600ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to improve liver function in chronic liver disease and to improve physical tiredness and general lassitude caused by impaired liver function.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have severe obstruction of the bile duct or fulminant hepatitis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; if you have large or small bowel inflammation such as Crohn's disease; if you have radio-opaque calcified gallstones, a non-functioning gallbladder or acute cholecystitis; if you have kidney disease; or if you have peptic ulcer (acute gastric or duodenal ulcer).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe pancreatic disease or gallstones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with an oral diabetes medicine (tolbutamide), cholestyramine, colestipol, medicinal charcoal, antacids containing magnesium or aluminium hydroxide, or medicines that increase cholesterol secretion from the liver (for example oral contraceptives containing oestrogen or lipid-lowering medicines such as clofibrate).

If diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn, stomach discomfort, itching, rash, general lassitude, dizziness, calcification of gallstones, raised liver enzyme values, reduced white blood cells or interstitial pneumonia (with fever, cough, difficulty breathing and abnormal chest X-ray) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Improving liver function in chronic liver disease and the physical tiredness and general lassitude caused by impaired liver function

groups.title: Capsule (101804ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For an acute condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day; children aged 6 to 14 years: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For a chronic condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day; children aged 6 to 14 years: take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis, children aged 6 years and older: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer, or if the user is a baby under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If you take it together with an oral antibiotic (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them. Avoid adding any other medicine to the solution of this medicine.

If, rarely, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, ringing in the ears, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), rapid heartbeat or high blood pressure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Solution (130502ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and itching of the skin.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 10 mg, 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 2 years to under 12 years: take 10 mg in 1 day if the body weight is 30 kg or more, and 5 mg in 1 day if the body weight is less than 30 kg. For people sensitive to adverse reactions, take it in divided doses in the morning and in the evening; the dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. In people with kidney impairment the dosing interval must be adjusted to kidney function, and in children with kidney impairment the dose must be adjusted individually according to renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a baby under 2 years of age; or if you have the rare hereditary defect of fructose intolerance.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (for example a spinal cord lesion or prostatic hyperplasia).

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, ritonavir or a large amount of alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drowsiness, headache; occasionally lassitude, numbness, weakness, agitation or abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary listlessness, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, movement disorder, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, loss of memory, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation or nightmares; occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, inflammation of the lips, taste disturbance or increased appetite; rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia or raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations or vasculitis; occasionally reduced white blood cells, reduced neutrophils, increased lymphocytes or increased eosinophils; rarely increased monocytes, increased or reduced platelets, or photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching or rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of eye accommodation or back-and-forth eye movement; vertigo; occasionally liver function disturbance such as raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, raised BUN, sugar in the urine or blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting or urinary retention; joint pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance or visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain.

Itching, urticaria and the like may appear after this medicine is stopped.

summaryTable.What it is for: Seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and itching of the skin

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A25000ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Those over 7 years of age and under 15 years of age: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby (newborn) under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), or cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (227735ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to remove bubbles in the bowel during gastroscopy, to remove gas in the bowel during abdominal X-ray examination, and to improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract, such as a feeling of fullness in the abdomen and aerophagia.
groups.usage: To remove bubbles in the bowel for gastroscopy, adults: take 40 to 80 mg with about 10 mL of water 15 to 40 minutes before the examination. To remove gas in the bowel for abdominal X-ray examination, adults: take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or between meals, starting 3 to 4 days before the examination. To improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract, adults: take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or at bedtime. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

The WHO-recommended acceptable daily intake is 40 mg of aspartame per kg of body weight per day or less. Use the smallest possible amount. For an adult weighing 60 kg the maximum in 1 day is 2.4 g.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are sensitive to sulfites or have asthma.

Shake it well before use.

If, occasionally, loose stools, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea, a feeling of heaviness in the abdomen or loss of appetite occurs, or if, rarely, headache occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

This medicine contains sodium benzoate. Benzoic acid may cause mild irritation of the skin, eyes and mucous membranes.

groups.title: Oral Solution (B04300ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as a tonic and for a weak constitution, physical tiredness, reduced strength after illness, loss of appetite, nutritional disturbance, and febrile and wasting disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains an ingredient derived from human placenta as its active ingredient. Pregnant women who agree to provide the human placenta used as the raw material are interviewed and confirmed to be free of infectious disease, and steps such as virus inactivation during manufacture are taken to prevent the transmission of infection; nevertheless, because it is made from human placenta as a raw material, take it only when the benefit outweighs the risk.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, or if you are taking a medicine containing levodopa.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are under the care of a doctor, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve or become worse after taking it for a period, consult a pharmacist. Use it by mouth only; do not use it for injection. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values.

Do not take it together with a medicine containing levodopa.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools or pharyngitis occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (106301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbance of mucus secretion.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day. When treatment is continued, take 1 tablet per dose, 2 times in 1 day. This medicine may be taken with or without food. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have severe kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are within the first 3 months of pregnancy; if you are breast-feeding; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, if you are an older person, or if you have kidney impairment or peptic ulcer.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If, very rarely, serious skin damage such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If nausea, purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count, or, uncommonly, vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain, heartburn, dry mouth, abnormal sensation of the tongue or a change in taste occurs, or if, rarely, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, constipation, loss of appetite, urticaria, skin rash, an anaphylactic reaction including anaphylactic shock, urticarial red spots (erythema), angioedema, itching or other hypersensitivity reactions, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, chills, numbness in the mouth or a feeling of numbness in the arm occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (101404ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, pain from a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 3 tablets (300 to 1000 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Up to 12 tablets (4000 mg) may be taken in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, reduced heart function or a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine); if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver impairment, kidney impairment, peptic ulcer, a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with another anti-inflammatory analgesic, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium, a thiazide diuretic, alcohol or flucloxacillin.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), high anion gap metabolic acidosis, raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child under 15 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had hypersensitivity to a cosmetic or to egg (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); or if you have an allergic constitution.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

If rash, reddening of the skin, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (symptoms such as fever, erythema, itching, red eyes or stomatitis, or severe symptoms such as rash and reddening with high fever and burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the membranes of the mouth and throat) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (268600ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is really necessary; if you have a constitution prone to allergy or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist. Those aged 7 years or younger should be given the syrup form. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (101804ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For an acute condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For a chronic condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis, ages 6 years and older: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer, or if the user is a baby under 2 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If you take it together with an oral antibiotic (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them. Avoid adding any other medicine to the solution of this medicine.

If, rarely, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, ringing in the ears, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), rapid heartbeat or high blood pressure occurs, or very rarely anaphylaxis occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for bowel regulation, constipation, loose stools, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen and abnormal fermentation in the intestine.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or between meals.
groups.caution:
This medicine must not be taken by a child aged 7 years or younger, or by anyone with a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
